The T20 scan trusts what it pins: the reviewed constants, the range checks behind PRAGMA busy_timeout (general-limit.js and connection.js are pinned only at the statement that takes the value), and allow-listed helpers only as far as their pinned text goes. Any reviewed edit to a pinned statement or helper needs a re-pin (the failure prints the new hash and the statement). It reads source, not behaviour.

The secrets scan reads files, not git history, and matches shapes: a live credential of an unknown shape in a recorded log would pass. The allow-list for the record (events.jsonl, state.json, one probe draft, one review) is by exact fragment: a future record that quotes another fake credential shape will need an entry. The e-mail and 32-character token rules are not applied to the whole project (hashes, slugs and reviewer addresses would match).
